name: Shoe size conversion
seoTitle: Shoe size conversion Calculator — Formula, Units & Example
seoDesc: Shoe size conversion: work out AU men / UK (0-15) from the US / CA / AU women. A free everyday life calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Shoe size conversion calculator returns AU men / UK (0-15) from the 3 fields on the form. No sign-up, no page reload, and the relationship behind it is printed below. Think of it as a shortcut for a practical question that turns up in daily life. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Shoe size conversion calculator work?
sections.html:
The Shoe size conversion calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports AU men / UK (0-15) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (adult or child?); then you type in the US / CA / AU women (1-15).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Shoe size conversion calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

AU men / UK (0-15)=3 × foot length in millimeters − 23
US / CA men (1-14)=3 × foot length in millimeters − 22
Foot length in millimeters=(1 ÷ 3) × US ÷ CA ÷ AU women (1-15) + 7
EU (33.5-50)=(127 ÷ 100) × AU men ÷ UK (0-15) + 3121 ÷ 100
Foot length in inches=(50 ÷ 127) × MX ÷ JP (19.5-32)
Foot length in inches=(5 ÷ 127) × korea (195-320)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Adult or child? set to Adult and Foot length in millimeters = 30 mm. Working through the relationship above gives US / CA (0.5-13.5) = -8.77, UK / AU (0-13.5) = -9, EU (15-32.5) = 3 and MX / JP (9-20) = 0.76.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: US / CA (0.5-13.5) = -8.77, UK / AU (0-13.5) = -9, EU (15-32.5) = 3 and MX / JP (9-20) = 0.76 should be roughly the size you expected from Adult or child? set to Adult and Foot length in millimeters = 30 mm.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Length, opening in millimeters
  • Length, opening in inches

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Shoe size conversion calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the US / CA / AU women — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Shoe size conversion calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns AU men / UK (0-15), derived from the US / CA / AU women. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Shoe size conversion calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the US / CA / AU women, which is 3 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter foot length in millimeters in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Foot length in millimeters opens in millimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports US / CA (0.5-13.5) = -8.77. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Shoe size conversion calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
